subject: Deployment mode Qs and legacy migration timeline
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sam Wu <sam.wu@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Lauren Kelly <lauren.kelly@acme-retail.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups from today's demo

Thanks again for taking the demo today, Sam — great discussion. Quick recap and items we need to qualify to propose the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem):

- Current preference you mentioned: low-latency customer-facing inference with EU data residency constraints and predictable throughput during peak hours.
- Migration situation: you have an existing integration with an LLM API (OpenAI) for the web app and an internal GPU cluster used for batch offline scoring.

Questions that will change our recommendation:
1) Expected steady-state QPS and peak QPS (or tokens/min) for the feature you plan to migrate (ballpark is fine).
2) Max acceptable tail latency (p95 / p99) for interactive calls.
3) Is the EU data residency requirement a hard block for hosted, or would a Dedicated pool in eu-west suffice?
4) Any strict procurement timeline or pilot start date we should align to?
5) Who is the procurement contact we should include for contract/compliance discussions?

I've attached a short one-pager that summarizes tradeoffs (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and a migration checklist that helps map steps from OpenAI/in-house clusters into a pilot. If you prefer, we can propose a Dedicated + Private VPC peering pilot (keeps workload isolated, predictable throughput) and a fallback to Hosted for overflow.

Next step: if you can send the QPS/latency numbers and procurement contact, I will share a proposed mutual action plan and preliminary pricing for a 90-day pilot.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-hosted-vs-dedicated-one-pager.pdf
From: Sam Wu <sam.wu@acme-retail.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Kelly <lauren.kelly@acme-retail.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups from today's demo

Appreciate the recap, Vivek. Answers inline:

1) Steady-state: ~250 requests/min (peak ~750–900 requests/min during promotions). Each request averages ~150 tokens in/out.
2) Target: p95 < 250ms, p99 < 400ms for interactive web experience.
3) EU residency is important for customer profile data; we would need the inference to run in eu-west for EU-origin requests. Hosted in a US-only region would not be acceptable.
4) Timeline: looking to start a pilot in early June and go to production in September (Q3).
5) Procurement/Legal contact: Lauren Kelly (cc'd) — procurement team prefers a short security questionnaire and a standard SOW.

Notes: we currently use OpenAI for real-time calls and spin up in-house GPU jobs overnight for batch enrichment. For the pilot, we're evaluating options that reduce per-token cost and give us more control over latencies. Curious about your data retention controls for Dedicated vs Private and whether Redwood supports on-prem connectors for air-gapped cases.

--
Sam Wu
Head of AI Product, Acme Retail
sam.wu@acme-retail.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-23T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups from today's demo

FYI — forwarding Sam's reply. Key migration signals:
- Steady 250 r/min, peaks ~900 r/min; per-request ~150 tokens.
- EU residency requirement (need eu-west for EU traffic).
- Pilot goal: early June; prod Sept.
- Current stack: OpenAI + on-prem GPU cluster.

Action items:
- Marissa: can you put together a 90-day MA plan and pricing for a Dedicated pool with optional Private VPC peering (eu-west) and an overflow policy to Hosted? Please include: reserved capacity sizing (GPU-equivalents), estimated tokens/month, and any discount tiers tied to commit. Attach migration-checklist.xlsx to your proposal.
- Aditya: need a short technical ops note on migration patterns from OpenAI + legacy clusters: data transfer strategy, KV/cache warmup, and whether we recommend prefix caching vs full KV pre-warm. Also call out any quantization or batch size changes we should recommend for their avg token length.

Copying Sam's email below. I'll follow up with procurement after we have a draft MA plan.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Wu <sam.wu@acme-retail.com>, Lauren Kelly <lauren.kelly@acme-retail.com>
Date: 2027-05-24T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups from today's demo

Thanks — drafted a concise mutual action plan and preliminary pricing below. Attaching migration-checklist.xlsx as discussed.

90-day pilot proposal (summary):
- Environment: Redwood Dedicated pool (eu-west) with Private VPC peering to Acme network for EU traffic; Hosted fallback for overflow.
- Sizing: reserve capacity to handle 1,000 r/min steady with 3x burst headroom (recommend 4x A100-equivalent GPUs for the pool).
- Observability: token-level billing enabled, per-route latency dashboards, and exportable audit logs for SOC2 evidence.
- Security: customer-managed KMS + VPC peering; data retention policy configurable (default 30 days, can be set to 0 for no retention).
- Pricing: pilot blended rate — $X,XXX/month reserved + $Y per million tokens overage. Discount tiers on 6/12-month commit.
- Deliverables & timeline:
  * Week 0: Kickoff + security questionnaire (Lauren)
  * Week 1–2: VPC peering + Dedicated pool provisioning (eu-west)
  * Week 3: Ingest and warm KV cache from in-house jobs; validate performance targets
  * Week 4–10: Pilot validation and SLA tuning
  * Post-week 12: Production cutover plan (Sept target)

Open questions for pricing/commit: what discount threshold do we need to offer to win the commitment? Also need Aditya's input on cache-warm and quantization tradeoffs for their token size.

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: migration-checklist.xlsx
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sam Wu <sam.wu@acme-retail.com>, Lauren Kelly <lauren.kelly@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-25T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed mutual action plan & next steps (pilot kickoff window)

Sam / Lauren — thanks for the clear answers. Based on the inputs, proposed next steps to align calendars and procurement: 

- We propose a Dedicated pilot in eu-west with Private VPC peering for EU traffic, plus Hosted overflow in other regions.
- Kickoff target: Week of 2027-06-01. High-level MA plan attached in Drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-redwood-pilot-plan
- Deliverables for kickoff: signed SOW (Lauren), completed security questionnaire, VPC peering details, and token budget for pilot.
- Technical owner meetings: schedule two 60-min sessions with Aditya/RW infra during Week 1 to map data movement from in-house cluster and API integration points.

I'll draft the SOW and a pilot statement of work and share by EOD tomorrow. Marissa — let's finalize pricing and commit thresholds; Aditya — ping me when you have the cache-warm recommendation.

If that timeline works for procurement, Lauren, please confirm and share the best time for a short procurement kickoff.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
